senses: Having two or more independent but harmonic melodies.
Able to play more than one musical note at the same time.
Capable of being read in more than one way.
ety: Originally from Ancient Greek πολύφωνος (polúphōnos) + -ic. In later use from poly- + -phonic.

senses: A planet located near the edge or rim of a galaxy.
examples: The traffic chief shook his head. "You're making a mistake. You should stay up in the rimworlds where the Orchestra is loved. Downsystem you're nothing."

senses: The property of being clearly discernible
The state or quality of being clear or bright; brightness; conspicuousness.
A disrespectful levity or pertness especially in respect to grave or sacred matters.
Respectful of the duties and attitudes of sons or daughters toward their parents.
ety: From Middle English filial, from Latin fīliālis, from fīlius (“son”) / fīlia (“daughter”) + -al.

senses: Intended to recompense someone who has experienced loss, suffering, or injury.
Reducing or offsetting the unpleasant or unwelcome effects of something.
ety: Borrowed from French compensatoire. By surface analysis, compensate + -ory.

senses: A dividend; a share or portion.
Congratulatory; that is giving congratulations.
Gratifying; pleasing.
examples: Mrs. Buckle was delivered of twins. "A pair of Buckles!" "Boys or girls?" inquired a congratulating friend the answer may be supposed.
His face grew sadder as the ceremony proceeded, and at last when the bride left the church, surrounded by a congratulating crowd, his eyes assumed the fixed look of a doomed man.

His great cause had been won; his client had been honorably acquitted; and there gathered around Mr. Storrs at the Lindell Hotel a congratulating circle, including many eminent members of the St. Louis bar.

senses: A plasma globulin of high molecular weight
A console that appears to support a cornice.
ety: From Latin ancōn, from Ancient Greek ἀγκών (ankṓn, “bend, elbow, cranny”).

senses: A communal bathhouse in Islamic countries and communities.
ety: Borrowed from Ottoman Turkish حمام (hamam), from Arabic حَمَّام (ḥammām).

senses: One who manufactures guns.
examples: This is like gunmakers coming out with bullets that contain eight essential vitamins.

senses: A person or thing that crunches.
living with the family of the husband.
In which newly married couples live with the husband's family.
examples: In barring the way, he is enacting a ritual which demands that the new way of patrilocal marriage pay its respect to the more ancient way of matrilocal marriage.

senses: A bathing suit composed of a tank top and the lower half of a bikini.
Argumentative or combative.
ety: From Middle English litigious, from Latin lītigiōsus. Compare Middle French litigieux.

senses: Prior claim (on payment, or on purchasing something); the first rights to obtain a particular payment or product.
Advancement to a higher position or office; promotion.
A position (especially in the Church of England) that provides profit or prestige.
ety: From Middle English preferment, preferrement, prefferment; equivalent to prefer + -ment.

senses: The office of an emir.
ety: From emir + -ate (forms nouns denoting rank or office, the concrete charge of it).

senses: A person who conforms; a conformist.
Characteristic of, or serving as a substitute
Engaging in completionism.
examples: M did not have this completionist fetish regarding other matters—he would happily leave a meal uneaten and a book half read—but in matters of travel it was something of a matter of pride.

Visiting the site was part of a completionist project engaged by many Johnny Cash fans, who wanted to see all the places associated with him, but for some, it was enough to glimpse it without leaving the car.

senses: A German sergeant.
An amphibious vehicle.
That which minimizes.
ety: From minimize + -er. In the linguistics sense, coined by American linguist Dwight Bolinger in 1972.

senses: Able to be excluded.
The rock of an elvan vein, or the vein itself.
ety: From a Cornish word, perhaps Cornish elven, elvan (“spark”) because the hard rock could be struck to spark fire.

senses: An incorrect or unwise investment.
examples: It is painful for the owners of malinvestments but fast and efficient.

senses: Without the use of solder.
The person who wins the bidding and so declares what suit will be trump.
ety: From Middle English declarer, equivalent to declare + -er.

senses: A user of the social media service Musical.ly.
ety: Likely a blend of Musical.ly (or music/musical) + user.
examples: With cool features for searching for content, sharing your own videos, and remixing work from other musers, there’s terrific potential here for an exciting, creative space for making music.
Musical.ly allows fans to send gifts to their favorite livestreaming musers which equate to actual cash.
In the context of musical.ly, “musers” produce and share videos, and inspire others to produce similar videos of the same song, using the same hand gestures or creating new performances.

senses: Any substance that inhibits the reabsorption of cations, especially sodium, from urine.
ety: From international scientific vocabulary, from New Latin, from natriuresis + -etic = natr- + -i- + uresis + etic; the combining forms are ultimately from New Latin natrium (“sodium”) + Ancient Greek οὔρησις (oúrēsis, “a making water”).

senses: To sulk or mope.
Tending to corrupt.
examples: So the exotic writer of Modernia prepares a reeking corruptive dish for his readers, o.r else an anaesthetic concocted from the malodorous flowers of the night.

senses: A loose, informal Japanese coat normally decorated with a distinctive crest.
The quality or state of being inviolable; inviolableness.
ety: From Middle French inviolabilité, from Latin inviolabilitas.
examples: Presidential acts of forgiveness in America seldom rattle confidence in the integrity of the judicial system or the inviolability of the rule of law.

senses: Synonym of flusherman.
The mechanical part of a flush toilet (e.g., a pullchain or lever) that causes the bowl's contents to be conveyed down the drain.
A worker for a political campaign who encourages voters to vote on Election Day.
ety: From Middle English flusshere. By surface analysis, flush + -er. First attested in the late 13th c.
examples: Each flusher is typically paid $20 to $50. Fleets of cars, buses, and other vehicles are also at the ready to ferry voters to and from the polls.

senses: To make or become smoked or smoky.
Growing, increasing, gaining size, etc.
Crescent-shaped.
ety: From crescent (“(growing) half moon”) + -ic. More at crescent.
examples: Twin dimples of the crescentic type came down her tanned cheeks on the sides of her mournful mouth.

senses: To work (a horse) in a circle at the end of a long line or rope.
ety: From French allonger (“to lengthen”), or Latin longa (“long”), i.e. the long rope.

senses: Divided into a line of squares of alternating tinctures.
ety: From French componé, from Old French compondre, from Latin compōnere (“put together, arrange, compile”). Cognate with English compose, compound.
